definition_en: to persuade by flattery, sweet talk or gentle urging
core_image: 摊主把一颗糖塞进孩子手里，孩子乖乖就范
scene: 集市上，摊主笑着把糖果塞给孩子。The vendor cajoled the child into tasting the cheese.
sceneCN: 这里 cajole 是「哄劝、甜言诱使」（第 1 个义项：以好话劝诱）；句意是摊主哄着孩子尝了那块奶酪。

derivatives.zh: 由 cajole 加 -ery 构成，义为「哄骗；甜言蜜语」
由动词加 -ing 转名词，义为「哄劝的行为」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「哄诱」

senses.title: To persuade by sweet talk
senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something by flattery or gentle deception
senses.definitionCN: 以奉承或温和的欺骗劝使某人做某事
senses.example: She cajoled her father into lending the car.
senses.exampleCN: 她哄得父亲把车借给了她。
senses.why: The French source literally meant to chatter like a jay.
senses.whyCN: 法语源词本义是「像松鸦一样喋喋不休」。

senses.title: To coax with persistence
senses.definition: to urge gently and persistently until agreement is won
senses.definitionCN: 以温和而持续的方式劝说得对方同意
senses.example: He cajoled and pleaded until the guard gave in.
senses.exampleCN: 他又哄又求，直到卫兵让步。
senses.why: Sweet talk repeated long enough wears down resistance.
senses.whyCN: 好话说得够久，抵抗便被磨平。

senses.title: To obtain by coaxing
senses.definition: to get something from someone by coaxing
senses.definitionCN: 用哄劝的方式从某人处取得
senses.example: The reporter cajoled a quote from the shy poet.
senses.exampleCN: 记者哄得那位腼腆诗人说了句引语。
senses.why: The act extends to the prize it wins.
senses.whyCN: 哄劝的行为延伸到它赢得的战利品。

intro.en: Cajole descends from French cajoler, to chatter like a jay in a cage, a bird of sweet nonsense.
intro.cn: cajole 源自法语 cajoler（如笼中松鸦般喋喋），像那只会说甜话的鸟。

items.en: behind Latin gaius, a jay, stands a reconstructed root for brightness or colour, uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaius（松鸦）背后是表「鲜亮、色彩」的重构词根，细节不确定。

items.en: gaius named the jay, the chattering bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaius 指松鸦，那种爱聒噪的鸟。

items.en: gaiole, a cage, and jaiole tied the bird to its cage.
items.cn: 古法语 gaiole（笼子）与松鸦结缘。

items.en: cajoler came to mean to chatter, then to coax with sweet chatter.
items.cn: 法语 cajoler 由「喋喋」转指「以甜言哄劝」。

items.en: English borrowed cajole for insinuating persuasion.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 cajole，指花言巧语的劝诱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cajoler family; the near-meaning group gathers persuasion words.
note.cn: 形近组是 cajoler 同族；近义组是劝说类词。

entries.definition: to flatter in order to persuade
to win over by reasoning or urging

normalIntro.en: A jay in a cage chatters sweet nonsense until you give in.
normalIntro.cn: 笼中松鸦甜言聒噪，直到你缴械。

normal.en: French cajoler means to chatter like a jay.
normal.cn: 法语 cajoler 意为像松鸦般喋喋。

normal.en: Cajole into is the key structure.
Cajolery is the noun of sweet talk.
normal.cn: cajolery 是「甜言蜜语」的名词。
coax 是更温和的近义词。

abstract.en: Hear a parrot repeat your name until you smile.
abstract.cn: 听鹦鹉一遍遍叫你的名字，直到你笑出声。

abstract.en: See an aunt press a second helping of cake on you.
abstract.cn: 看姑姑非再给你添一块蛋糕不可。

abstract.en: Feel resistance soften under a stream of compliments.
abstract.cn: 感受抵抗力在一连串恭维下慢慢软化。

examples.en: The negotiator cajoled both sides back to the table.
examples.cn: 谈判者连哄带劝把双方劝回谈判桌。

examples.en: Grandmother cajoled the secret out of him at last.
examples.cn: 祖母最终哄出了他的秘密。

examples.en: No amount of cajoling could change the verdict.
examples.cn: 再怎么哄劝也改变不了裁决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡·粥」——小孩不肯喝粥，妈妈好话说尽才把粥「喂」下去，一勺一勺哄。

root: cajole 源自法语 cajoler「像笼中松鸦般喋喋」，鸟笼 gaiole 与松鸦 gaia 相伴而生；甜言聒噪转指哄诱；同族词 cajolery（甜言蜜语）、cajolement（哄诱）皆由此展开。

sensesIntro.en: A caged bird's chatter becomes the human art of talking others round.
sensesIntro.cn: 笼中鸟的聒噪，化为人类「把人哄转」的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sweet chatter wearing a stubborn listener down.
core.cn: 核心意象：甜言软语磨平对方的固执。

branches.en: cajoled and pleaded till the guard gave in
cajoled a quote from the poet

intro.en: Cajole keeps the French verb whole; its English offspring simply add noun endings.
intro.cn: cajole 保留了完整的法语动词形；其英语派生词只添名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is the Latin jay gaius, via Old French cage words gaiole and jaiole.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语松鸦 gaius，经古法语笼词 gaiole、jaiole 而来。

items.meaning: to chatter like a caged jay; to coax
items.meaningCN: 如笼中松鸦般喋喋；哄劝
